gaps.sentence: I was nearly late, but I managed to ___ the last bus.
gaps.hint: to get on a bus or train in time
gaps.explanation: catch a bus/train means to arrive in time to board it; the words 'managed to' and 'nearly late' show success.

gaps.sentence: Try to ___ quiet — the exam is in progress.
gaps.explanation: keep quiet means to stay silent; 'make quiet' is not used.

gaps.sentence: The children were told not to ___ so much noise.
gaps.explanation: make a noise / make noise is the fixed collocation.

gaps.sentence: Stop ___ money on things you never use.
gaps.hint: to use money on useless things; -ing form after 'Stop'
gaps.explanation: waste money on something means to spend it on useless things; 'stop' is followed by the -ing form.

gaps.sentence: Her family has ___ a small hotel for thirty years.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'a hotel/business' meaning managed it
gaps.explanation: run a business/hotel means to manage or operate it; the past participle is needed after 'has'.

gaps.sentence: Please ___ your seats; the performance is about to begin.
gaps.explanation: take your seats is the formal way of asking people to sit down.

gaps.sentence: Students should ___ attention when the teacher is speaking.
gaps.explanation: pay attention is the fixed collocation for listening or concentrating carefully.

gaps.sentence: He didn't ___ any interest in politics until university.
gaps.explanation: take an interest in something means to become curious or involved in it.
